title: Resting-State EEG and Trait Anxiety
description: This dataset comprises resting-state EEG recordings from 51 right-handed undergraduate participants collected at the University of Alberta, examining relationships between alpha/theta oscillatory dynamics and trait anxiety. Recordings include alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed resting blocks, accompanied by anxiety and personality questionnaire data. The dataset supports investigation into EEG correlates of trait anxiety and related psychological constructs.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a 256-channel EGI HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net with a Net Amps amplifier at an original sampling rate of 500 Hz, referenced online to Cz. Participants completed a resting-state protocol of alternating 1-minute eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks (EO-EC-EO-EC) for 4 minutes total, with auditory cues signaling transitions. Preprocessing in EEGLAB included 0.1-50 Hz bandpass filtering, CleanLine noise removal at 60/120 Hz, kurtosis-based channel rejection, average re-referencing, ICA decomposition (runica), ICLabel-based artifact removal (>0.8 probability) with visual inspection, and spherical interpolation of removed channels.
